topic.title: Prediction-Assisted Statistical Inference and Evaluation
topic.overview: Machine-learning predictions can fill gaps in expensive or incomplete observations, but treating those predictions as measured truth can invalidate statistical conclusions. This topic combines predictive models with inference procedures that account for their errors, selection bias, and adaptive data collection. It also examines how evaluation can reveal unreliable estimates or forecasts.
topic.whyItMatters: The aim is to extract useful information from abundant unlabeled data without sacrificing valid uncertainty statements. Better prediction does not automatically guarantee unbiased scientific inference, especially when the data were selected adaptively or the target population differs from the observed sample.
topic.evolution: Earlier representatives concern likelihood fitting and cross-validation. Recent work focuses on calibration, selection bias, and post-prediction analysis. PSPS in 2024 provides a task-agnostic framework for integrating predicted outcomes with established analyses; a 2026 adaptive-inference method combines predictions and labeled bandit data with asymptotic guarantees under conditions on the collection policy.
openQuestions: When can predictions improve inferential efficiency without adding hidden selection bias?
How should uncertainty account for repeated adaptation of both models and sampling policies?

papers.title: On Least Square Estimation in Softmax Gating Mixture of Experts
papers.tldr: Strong identifiability explains why least-squares estimation can converge much faster for sigmoid and tanh experts than for polynomial experts.

papers.title: Performance Bounds for Active Binary Testing with Information Maximization
papers.tldr: InfoMax receives tight near-optimal testing guarantees when a sufficiently balanced binary test remains available at every step.

papers.title: Position: Embracing Negative Results in Machine Learning
papers.tldr: The paper argues that normalizing negative results would improve research incentives and broaden how machine learning publications are valued.

papers.title: PriorBoost: An Adaptive Algorithm for Learning from Aggregate Responses
papers.tldr: PriorBoost adaptively groups samples with increasingly similar hidden responses to improve individual predictions learned from aggregate labels.

papers.title: Relaxed Quantile Regression: Prediction Intervals for Asymmetric Noise
papers.tldr: Relaxed Quantile Regression improves prediction-interval flexibility and width while retaining quantile regression's coverage guarantees.

papers.title: Rethinking Data Shapley for Data Selection Tasks: Misleads and Merits
papers.tldr: Data Shapley can match random selection without utility constraints, but selects optimally for an identified class of structured utility functions.

papers.title: Risk Aware Benchmarking of Large Language Models
papers.tldr: Risk-aware benchmarking compares distributions of metric portfolios with statistical significance instead of relying only on average scores.

papers.title: Sampling-based Multi-dimensional Recalibration
papers.tldr: A sample-based recalibration method accounts for dependencies between outputs and guarantees calibration under a highest-density-region criterion.

papers.title: Scaling Laws for the Value of Individual Data Points in Machine Learning
papers.tldr: Individual training examples follow different value-scaling patterns, making their relative usefulness depend on dataset size.

papers.title: Sequential Kernel Goodness-of-fit Testing
papers.tldr: A betting-based sequential goodness-of-fit test adapts evidence gathering to problem difficulty while controlling false rejections.

papers.title: Statistical Inference Under Constrained Selection Bias
papers.tldr: Known expectations in a target population constrain selection bias and enable high-probability bounds on quantities of interest.

papers.title: Statistical Properties of Robust Satisficing
papers.tldr: The paper establishes statistical guarantees for Robust Satisficing and reports practical advantages with limited data and distribution shifts.

papers.title: TIC-TAC: A Framework For Improved Covariance Estimation In Deep Heteroscedastic Regression
papers.tldr: TIC-TAC uses local derivatives to improve covariance prediction and introduces an evaluation metric, with reported gains in covariance accuracy and training convergence.

papers.title: Total Variation Floodgate for Variable Importance Inference in Classification
papers.tldr: Total Variation Floodgate provides asymptotic lower confidence bounds for a model-free classification importance measure under design-based or model-X assumptions.

papers.title: 2D-OOB: Attributing Data Contribution Through Joint Valuation Framework
papers.tldr: 2D-OOB jointly values training examples and their individual cells to identify which pieces of data help or harm a model.

papers.title: Active, anytime-valid risk controlling prediction sets
papers.tldr: The method builds prediction sets with risk guarantees that remain valid over time while selectively requesting labels within an expected budget.

papers.title: Data Distribution Valuation
papers.tldr: The paper uses MMD to compare the value of data-generating distributions from samples under a specified model of vendor heterogeneity.

papers.title: Distributional regression: CRPS-error bounds for model fitting, model selection and convex aggregation
papers.tldr: The paper derives CRPS error and regret bounds for fitting, selecting, and combining distributional regression models under independent, identically distributed sampling.

papers.title: Distributionally Robust Performative Prediction
papers.tldr: A robust performative-prediction framework accounts for errors in modeling how deployed predictions change future data.

papers.title: DU-Shapley: A Shapley Value Proxy for Efficient Dataset Valuation
papers.tldr: DU-Shapley uses dataset-valuation structure to approximate Shapley values more efficiently, supported by theory and numerical experiments.

papers.title: Information-theoretic Generalization Analysis for Expected Calibration Error
papers.tldr: The paper bounds bias in binned calibration estimates and derives informative generalization bounds for expected calibration error.

papers.title: Is Cross-validation the Gold Standard to Estimate Out-of-sample Model Performance?
papers.tldr: Across the analyzed model classes, cross-validation offers limited or no statistical advantage over training-data plug-in estimates of out-of-sample performance.

papers.title: Is Score Matching Suitable for Estimating Point Processes?
papers.tldr: A consistent weighted score-matching estimator addresses failures of earlier point-process estimators while avoiding intensity integrals.

papers.title: Most Influential Subset Selection: Challenges, Promises, and Beyond
papers.tldr: Influence-based subset selection can fail because examples interact, while iterative adaptation partially addresses the problem at a computational cost.

papers.title: One Sample Fits All: Approximating All Probabilistic Values Simultaneously and Efficiently
papers.tldr: A shared sampling framework efficiently approximates multiple probabilistic attribution values and also solves a related family of datamodels.

papers.title: Optimal Algorithms for Augmented Testing of Discrete Distributions
papers.tldr: Prediction-assisted distribution tests adaptively save samples while preserving standard sample guarantees when predictions are poor.

papers.title: Real-Time Selection Under General Constraints via Predictive Inference
papers.tldr: The paper proposes an online selection rule that uses prediction uncertainty to control individual and interactive constraints together.

papers.title: Scaling laws for learning with real and surrogate data
papers.tldr: An approximate scaling law helps choose how much surrogate data to add and how strongly to weight it for improved target-distribution predictions.

papers.title: Sigmoid Gating is More Sample Efficient than Softmax Gating in Mixture of Experts
papers.tldr: Under the analyzed regression and identifiability conditions, sigmoid gating estimates experts more sample-efficiently than softmax gating.

papers.title: Stratified Prediction-Powered Inference for Effective Hybrid Evaluation of Language Models
papers.tldr: StratPPI uses stratified sampling to obtain valid confidence intervals that can be substantially tighter with appropriate grouping and sample allocation.

papers.title: Task-Agnostic Machine-Learning-Assisted Inference
papers.tldr: PSPS enables valid, efficient statistical inference from machine-learning-predicted outcomes through broad compatibility with existing analysis routines.

papers.title: Testing Calibration in Nearly-Linear Time
papers.tldr: A structured flow formulation enables an information-theoretically optimal calibration test running in O(n log² n) time.

papers.title: Training Data Attribution via Approximate Unrolling
papers.tldr: Source uses approximate training unrolling to estimate data-removal effects efficiently, improving attribution for non-converged models and multistage training.

papers.title: Treeffuser: probabilistic prediction via conditional diffusions with gradient-boosted trees
papers.tldr: Treeffuser combines conditional diffusion with gradient-boosted trees to produce flexible, well-calibrated predictive distributions for tabular data.

papers.title: Truthfulness of Calibration Measures
papers.tldr: SSCE measures calibration while making truthful sequential forecasting optimal up to a constant factor.

papers.title: Using Noise to Infer Aspects of Simplicity Without Learning
papers.tldr: Theoretical results connect several forms of data noise with the availability of simpler models among near-optimal alternatives.

papers.title: When is Multicalibration Post-Processing Necessary?
papers.tldr: A broad empirical study finds that multicalibration post-processing helps some models, while already calibrated predictors often need less additional correction.

papers.title: Zipper: Addressing Degeneracy in Algorithm-Agnostic Inference
papers.tldr: Zipper uses overlapping evaluation splits to avoid degenerate model-comparison statistics and support valid asymptotic testing with effective data reuse.

papers.title: A Novel Characterization of the Population Area Under the Risk Coverage Curve (AURC) and Rates of Finite Sample Estimators
papers.tldr: The paper expresses population AURC as reweighted risk and develops finite-sample estimators with proven convergence guarantees.

papers.title: e-GAI: e-value-based Generalized $α$-Investing for Online False Discovery Rate Control
papers.tldr: e-GAI dynamically allocates testing levels using valid e-values to improve power while maintaining provable online false discovery rate control.

papers.title: Geometric Median (GM) Matching for Robust k-Subset Selection from Noisy Data
papers.tldr: GM Matching selects subsets whose means approximate a geometric median, improving theoretical convergence and empirical pruning performance on noisy data.

papers.title: Importance Sampling for Nonlinear Models
papers.tldr: Generalized nonlinear norm and leverage scores enable importance sampling with approximation guarantees and applications to training, explanation, and outlier detection.

papers.title: Learning Survival Distributions with the Asymmetric Laplace Distribution
papers.tldr: The method learns individualized Asymmetric Laplace survival distributions, yielding closed-form event-time summaries and strong reported predictive performance.

papers.title: MissScore: High-Order Score Estimation in the Presence of Missing Data
papers.tldr: MissScore estimates higher-order distributional scores from incomplete data using objectives tailored to different missing-data mechanisms.

papers.title: Off-Policy Evaluation under Nonignorable Missing Data
papers.tldr: The paper analyzes missing-data bias in off-policy evaluation and proposes inverse probability weighting with uncertainty quantification.

papers.title: On the Impact of Performative Risk Minimization for Binary Random Variables
papers.tldr: In a binary-variable setting with linear performative shifts, optimizing for prediction-induced changes can amplify side effects compared with methods that ignore them.

papers.title: PAC-Bayes Analysis for Recalibration in Classification
papers.tldr: A PAC-Bayes calibration bound motivates a generalization-aware algorithm that improves Gaussian-process-based recalibration in experiments.

papers.title: Pairwise Maximum Likelihood For Multi-Class Logistic Regression Model With Multiple Rare Classes
papers.tldr: Separate rare-versus-majority logistic regressions can match joint estimation’s asymptotic efficiency under suitable conditions while enabling cheaper, parallel computation.

papers.title: Prediction models that learn to avoid missing values
papers.tldr: Missingness-avoiding training reduces dependence on unavailable feature values while maintaining competitive predictive performance.

papers.title: Prediction-Powered Adaptive Shrinkage Estimation
papers.tldr: Prediction-Powered Adaptive Shrinkage combines within-task prediction debiasing with cross-task shrinkage and an asymptotically optimal tuning strategy.

papers.title: Prediction-Powered E-Values
papers.tldr: The framework gives e-value-based inference procedures prediction-powered counterparts while retaining their sequential and validity benefits.

papers.title: Prediction via Shapley Value Regression
papers.tldr: ViaSHAP learns feature attributions whose sum gives predictions, achieving competitive tabular performance and more accurate explanations than FastSHAP.

papers.title: QuEst: Enhancing Estimates of Quantile-Based Distributional Measures Using Model Predictions
papers.tldr: QuEst combines observed data and model predictions to estimate diverse quantile-based measures with rigorous confidence intervals.

papers.title: R.I.P.: Better Models by Survival of the Fittest Prompts
papers.tldr: RIP filters training prompts using rejected-response quality and preference reward gaps, yielding reported gains over unfiltered datasets.

papers.title: Regression for the Mean: Auto-Evaluation and Inference with Few Labels through Post-hoc Regression
papers.tldr: A regression view explains PPI++ failures with very few labels and motivates two robust-regression techniques with lower estimator variance.

papers.title: Risk and cross validation in ridge regression with correlated samples
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes ridge-regression risk under correlated samples and derives corrected cross-validation estimators under stated correlation assumptions.

papers.title: The Value of Prediction in Identifying the Worst-Off
papers.tldr: The paper develops frameworks for comparing prediction with administrative capacity when government programs aim to identify and assist the worst-off.

papers.title: Understanding Fixed Predictions via Confined Regions
papers.tldr: Finding confined feature-space regions exposes fixed predictions for future individuals that dataset-based, person-by-person audits can miss.

papers.title: A Unified Framework for Provably Efficient Algorithms to Estimate Shapley Values
papers.tldr: A unified framework supplies finite-sample guarantees for KernelSHAP and related estimators, alongside practical improvements for estimating feature contributions.

papers.title: Anytime-valid, Bayes-assisted, Prediction-Powered Inference
papers.tldr: Prediction-powered confidence sequences incorporate prior knowledge of prediction quality and provide asymptotic validity uniformly over time as data accumulate.

papers.title: Beyond Benign Overfitting in Nadaraya-Watson Interpolators
papers.tldr: A classical interpolating estimator exhibits several distinct generalization regimes as one parameter changes.

papers.title: Conditional Forecasts and Proper Scoring Rules for Reliable and Accurate Performative Predictions
papers.tldr: The paper establishes conditions for well-defined performative forecasts and identifies scoring approaches that can elicit correct predictions.

papers.title: Faithful Group Shapley Value
papers.tldr: Faithful Group Shapley Value resists inflated valuations from strategic group splitting and comes with a fast, accurate approximation algorithm.

papers.title: Final-Model-Only Data Attribution with a Unifying View of Gradient-Based Methods
papers.tldr: The paper unifies gradient-based data attribution as approximations to model sensitivity measured through further training of the final model.

papers.title: Introducing FOReCAst: The Future Outcome Reasoning and Confidence Assessment Benchmark
papers.tldr: FOReCAst evaluates forecasting accuracy and confidence calibration across yes-or-no outcomes, timeframe predictions, and quantity estimates.

papers.title: KAIROS: Scalable Model-Agnostic Data Valuation
papers.tldr: KAIROS values training examples through MMD against a clean reference distribution, improving reported valuation quality and achieving up to 15-fold speedup.

papers.title: On Minimax Estimation of Parameters in Softmax-Contaminated Mixture of Experts
papers.tldr: Parameter estimation in softmax-contaminated mixtures of experts slows substantially when the trainable prompt becomes difficult to distinguish from the pretrained model.

papers.title: On the Hardness of Conditional Independence Testing In Practice
papers.tldr: The paper links practical conditional independence testing failures to conditional estimation errors and a kernel-choice tension between detection power and false positives.

papers.title: PAC-Bayes Bounds for Multivariate Linear Regression and Linear Autoencoders
papers.tldr: The paper develops practical PAC-Bayes generalization bounds for multi-output linear regression and, under stated conditions, linear autoencoders.

papers.title: Performative Risk Control: Calibrating Models for Reliable Deployment under Performativity
papers.tldr: Performative Risk Control iteratively calibrates models with theoretical risk guarantees when prediction-supported decisions influence subsequent outcomes.

papers.title: Regression-adjusted Monte Carlo Estimators for Shapley Values and Probabilistic Values
papers.tldr: The method combines Monte Carlo sampling with flexible regression models to produce unbiased, more accurate estimates of probabilistic contribution values.

papers.title: Rescaled Influence Functions: Accurate Data Attribution in High Dimension
papers.tldr: Rescaled influence functions improve estimates of training-data effects in high dimensions with little added computational cost.

papers.title: Risk Bounds For Distributional Regression
papers.tldr: The paper derives risk bounds for constrained distributional regression, including isotonic, trend-filtering, and neural-network estimators.

papers.title: Smooth Sailing: Lipschitz-Driven Uncertainty Quantification for Spatial Associations
papers.tldr: The method provides confidence intervals for spatial associations under smoothness and constant-variance Gaussian error assumptions, without requiring model correctness.

papers.title: Statistical Inference under Performativity
papers.tldr: A new inference framework supports uncertainty estimates when prediction-informed decisions change the outcomes being predicted.

papers.title: Taming Hyperparameter Sensitivity in Data Attribution: Practical Selection Without Costly Retraining
papers.tldr: The paper reveals widespread hyperparameter sensitivity in data attribution and derives a retraining-free way to select regularization for influence-function methods.

papers.title: $\texttt{BetaConform}$: Efficient MAP Estimation of LLM Ensemble Judgment Performance with Prior Transfer
papers.tldr: BetaConform combines Bayesian estimation, adaptive sampling, and transferred priors to estimate LLM ensemble-judge performance with few labeled examples.

papers.title: The Bias-Variance Tradeoff in Data-Driven Optimization: A Local Misspecification Perspective
papers.tldr: Local misspecification reveals how decision bias and variance shape the relative performance of three data-driven optimization approaches.

papers.title: The Impact of Coreset Selection on Spurious Correlations and Group Robustness
papers.tldr: Coreset selection can alter bias and group robustness in different ways, with tiny prototypical subsets sometimes hiding weak group performance.

papers.title: Unveiling Extraneous Sampling Bias with Data Missing-Not-At-Random
papers.tldr: SuperDR addresses bias that persists in existing doubly robust estimators when training and test units differ despite sharing a feature–rating distribution.

papers.title: Valid Inference with Imperfect Synthetic Data
papers.tldr: A hyperparameter-free estimator combines real and imperfect synthetic data, improving estimation when their moment residuals are predictive of one another.

papers.title: When Models Don’t Collapse: On the Consistency of Iterative MLE
papers.tldr: Iterative maximum likelihood training can avoid collapse under suitable assumptions, but retaining original data and ordinary consistency alone do not suffice.

papers.title: YEAST: Yet Another Sequential Test
papers.tldr: YEAST derives a continuously monitored A/B test from threshold-crossing bounds and outperforms existing sequential tests in semi-synthetic simulations.

papers.title: A Strictly Proper Scoring Rule and a Calibration Metric for Interval-Censored Data Analysis
papers.tldr: The paper separates key interval-censoring assumptions and introduces assumption-specific tools for scoring and calibrating event-time predictions.

papers.title: Active Budget Allocation for Efficient Scaling Law Estimation via Surrogate-Guided Pruning
papers.tldr: Surrogate-guided allocation of training compute improves scaling-law estimation efficiency, with reported savings of up to 98.7% over exhaustive collection.

papers.title: An Odd Estimator for Shapley Values
papers.tldr: OddSHAP estimates Shapley values using only the mathematically relevant odd component, achieving leading accuracy at larger sampling budgets.

papers.title: Black-Box Assisted Regression: Phase Transitions and Minimax Optimality
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes when correcting a black-box predictor helps and proposes validation-based residual learning to avoid negative transfer.

papers.title: Frontier Models Can Take Actions at Low Probabilities
papers.tldr: Frontier models can accurately execute extremely rare actions under some conditions, exposing a potential weakness of limited-sample evaluations.

papers.title: Generalization of Gibbs and Langevin Monte Carlo Algorithms in the Interpolation Regime
papers.tldr: Data-dependent Gibbs error bounds use high-temperature training behavior to assess low-temperature generalization and remain stable under Langevin Monte Carlo approximation.

papers.title: Human-AI Collaborative Uncertainty Quantification
papers.tldr: Calibrated AI refinement of human prediction sets improves coverage–efficiency tradeoffs while accounting for harm and complementary corrections.

papers.title: Is Data Shapley Not Better than Random in Data Selection? Ask NASH
papers.tldr: NASH improves Shapley-based data selection by decomposing utility into informative components and combining them nonlinearly.

papers.title: MEC: Machine-Learning-Assisted Generalized Entropy Calibration for Semi-Supervised Mean Estimation
papers.tldr: MEC uses cross-fitting and calibration weights to improve semi-supervised mean estimation and confidence intervals under weaker assumptions.

papers.title: Minimizing Upper Confidence Bounds: A Data-Driven Framework for Stochastic Programming
papers.tldr: APUB optimization minimizes an upper confidence bound on expected cost to account for poorly known probability distributions.

papers.title: No Free Lunch: Non-Asymptotic Analysis of Prediction-Powered Inference
papers.tldr: Finite-sample analysis shows that PPI++ can worsen mean estimation unless pseudo-label correlation is high enough for the available labeled sample size.

papers.title: Nonparametric Distribution Regression Re-calibration
papers.tldr: A nonparametric recalibration method uses conditional kernel embeddings to improve predictive uncertainty across regression benchmarks and model classes.

papers.title: One-Shot Weighted Ensemble Estimation for Federated Quantile Regression: Optimal Statistical Guarantees under Heterogeneous Structured Data
papers.tldr: A one-shot weighted ensemble combines federated quantile models with different feature sets and provides statistical guarantees within the analyzed setting.

papers.title: Performative Learning Theory
papers.tldr: The paper derives generalization bounds for predictions that change their own data and identifies benefits from retraining on affected samples.

papers.title: Position: AI for Science Should Treat Measurement-to-Dataset Pipelines as Inference Components
papers.tldr: The authors argue that scientific measurement pipelines must become explicit, testable parts of inference because their choices shape both datasets and uncertainty.

papers.title: Predictable Compression Failures: Order Sensitivity and Information Budgeting for Evidence-Grounded Binary Adjudication
papers.tldr: An information-based framework predicts evidence-order sensitivity and supports a low-hallucination answer-or-abstain rule in a held-out binary-decision audit.

papers.title: Prediction-Powered Adaptive Inference with Pretrained AI Models for Contextual Bandits
papers.tldr: PPAI combines AI predictions with adaptive experiment data to improve asymptotic inference efficiency when predictions help, without worsening baseline asymptotic variance.

papers.title: Prediction-Powered Risk Monitoring of Deployed Models for Detecting Harmful Distribution Shifts
papers.tldr: PPRM combines synthetic and scarce true labels to detect harmful performance shifts with anytime-valid risk bounds and finite-sample false-alarm guarantees.

papers.title: Priority-Aware Shapley Value
papers.tldr: Priority-Aware Shapley Value combines precedence constraints and contributor-specific weights to make attribution reflect dependencies and priorities.

papers.title: ProEval: Proactive Failure Discovery and Efficient Performance Estimation for Generative AI Evaluation
papers.tldr: ProEval uses uncertainty-aware surrogate models to estimate performance with fewer tests while discovering more diverse failures.

papers.title: Robust Contextual Optimization with Missing Covariates
papers.tldr: The method makes robust contextual decisions directly from incomplete features by optimizing over distributions consistent with observed data and missingness structure.

papers.title: SciPredict: Can LLMs Predict the Outcomes of Scientific Experiments in Natural Sciences?
papers.tldr: SciPredict finds that tested LLMs predict scientific outcomes poorly and fail to identify their reliable predictions, even when outperforming experts overall.

papers.title: SCORE: A Unified Framework for Overshoot Refund in Online FDR Control
papers.tldr: SCORE recovers excess e-value evidence to improve online testing power while preserving finite-sample false discovery rate control.

papers.title: Semi-knockoffs: a model-agnostic conditional independence testing method with finite-sample guarantees
papers.tldr: Semi-knockoffs enables model-agnostic conditional independence testing without a train-test split, with finite-sample guarantees under its stated assumptions.

papers.title: Sequential Kernel-based Conditional Independence Testing via Adaptive Betting
papers.tldr: Adaptive betting and calibrated kernel statistics make sequential conditional independence testing more robust to estimated conditional distributions.

papers.title: Simultaneous Confidence Bounds for Aggregated Effects via Exact Subset Optimization
papers.tldr: Subset optimization enables tighter simultaneous confidence bounds for aggregated effects selected after observing independent test results.

papers.title: Temper-Then-Tilt: Principled Unlearning for Generative Models through Tempering and Classifier Guidance
papers.tldr: T3-Unlearning flattens a frozen model’s concentrated probability peaks before applying classifier guidance, improving forgetting and utility on TOFU.

papers.title: The Relative Instability of Model Comparison with Cross-validation
papers.tldr: Individually stable models can yield unstable comparisons and invalid cross-validation inference, so relative stability must be checked separately.

papers.title: When Can We Trust Survival Model Evaluation ?
papers.tldr: Censoring can distort survival-evaluation scores and model rankings in ways that depend on both its rate and mechanism.

papers.title: When More Experts Hurt: Underfitting in Multi-Expert Learning to Defer
papers.tldr: PiCCE addresses underfitting in multi-expert learning to defer by adaptively identifying a reliable expert from empirical evidence.

papers.title: When Sample Selection Bias Precipitates Model Collapse
papers.tldr: Filtering synthetic data against fragmented local references can accelerate model collapse, while collaborative proxy references mitigate diversity loss.
